findings.whyThisIsNotDigestDrift: The digest pin is correct. The file at that digest has not moved. The defect is the transcription: a REJECT is recorded as an ACCEPT. A reader who trusts recordedInputs and does not open the pinned bytes is told the v3 occupancy cleared independent review at 0/0 when it did not, and is told nothing about the one finding that is still standing on this exact lineage.
findings.netEffect: The subject inverts the two predecessor gradings it had available. The predecessor that earned ACCEPT 0/0 - v1, which sits at the promised path - has its review omitted entirely. The predecessor that was REJECTed - v3 - is presented as ACCEPT 0/0. This is the same provenance-honesty failure CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1 named against v3, now inverted and amplified rather than repaired.
findings.consequence: A later D-000 recording that pins this v4 occupancy would carry into the record a false statement about the independent standing of a frozen predecessor, sourced from a correctly-pinned artifact. Under DR-204's precedent that a coordinator-composed discharge is unlawful for a graded act, a misstated predecessor grade is not a hygiene item.
findings.fix: State the pinned review's actual standing: Claude REJECT at 0 blockers / 0 MUST-FIX / 1 SHOULD-FIX (CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1); Codex not reviewed. Separately cite harness.DR-G01.core-download.v1.review-independent.claude2.json at c2339ec6 with its true ACCEPT 0/0, since v1 is a cited predecessor and its grade is the one being borrowed. No change to the harness content is needed or permitted.

findings.title: basedOn.cghsV4.role re-asserts the exact claim CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1 adjudicated false under both readings, and carries neither of the two repairs that finding specified
findings.where: basedOn.cghsV4.role, with basedOn.predecessorV1.role as the compounding factor
findings.theClaim: "This v4 occupies the promised G01 artifact path against live HEAD."

measured.promisedPath: CGHS v4's DR-G01 entry carries artifactPathWhenAuthored = 'docs/coop/artifacts/harness.DR-G01.core-download.v1.json'.
measured.cghsV3G01EqualsCghsV4G01: True, by == object comparison. The G01 entry did not move between CGHS v3 and CGHS v4, so the promised path is unchanged from the state SF1 measured. (This is independently corroborated by CLAUDE-G03-V1-SF1's own evidence block, which records that the CGHS v3-to-v4 retarget was confined to G03's self-referential path field and that the DR-G01 entry is byte-identical between them.)
measured.thatFileIsUnmoved: v1 measured at 0ddb58cf, mode 0444 - equal to this subject's own predecessorV1 pin.
measured.thatFileCarriesTheSameHarness: v1's harness object == CGHS v4's DR-G01 entry, by == object comparison.

findings.whyTheClaimIsFalseUnderBothReadings: Read literally, v4 does not sit at the promised path and so cannot occupy it. Read loosely as 'an extraction pinned to the accepted parent now exists at the promised path', the condition already held before v4 was written, because v1 sits at that path and its harness object is equal to CGHS v4's live DR-G01 entry. This is the same two-reading refutation SF1 recorded against v3, and every premise of it was re-measured against live bytes for this subject rather than carried over.
findings.theCompoundingFactor: SF1's specified repair was to either (a) say what the successor adds over v1 and disclose that v1 occupies the promised path, already pins the accepted parent, and how a reader should choose between them, or (b) say v1 is superseded and explain why the promised path should now be read as pointing at a superseded file. The subject does neither. basedOn.predecessorV1.role reads in full: 'Frozen v1. Thin extraction predecessor. Unmoved. Not this artifact's version number.' It never states that v1 sits at the promised path, never states that v1 carries the byte-equal harness object, never states v1's ACCEPT 0/0, and never gives a reader a rule for choosing between v1 and v4.
findings.notEstoppedByHouseForm: This reviewer first considered declining this finding as inherited house language, since v1 and v3 both used the phrase and v3 sits off the promised path too. That reasoning fails: the phrase in v3 is precisely what SF1 charged, SF1 is unrepaired and unwithdrawn, and its repair text names a v4 as the artifact that would discharge it. A successor that repeats the charged sentence and omits the specified disclosure carries the finding forward rather than settling it.
findings.consequence: Four files now carry a DR-G01 harness object descended from the same accepted parent entry, and the parent's own pointer still names v1. SF1 recorded that this ambiguity is the precise thing the artifactPathWhenAuthored promise exists to prevent. This subject increases it by one while asserting it resolves it.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with what is true - that this v4 remasures occupancy of the unversioned identifier harness.DR-G01.core-download against live HEAD, which is what the rest of the subject already says correctly and repeatedly - and expand predecessorV1.role to disclose that v1 occupies CGHS v4's artifactPathWhenAuthored, carries the byte-equal harness object, holds Claude ACCEPT 0/0 at review digest c2339ec6, and how a reader should choose between v1 and this occupancy. No change to retainedEvidence or to any harness content is needed or permitted.
findings.whatIsNotWrong: The subject is otherwise scrupulous about lineage version independence: leftoverJoinV7.role and namingV6.role both state that those lineages' version numbers are unrelated to this one, and every predecessor role ends 'Not this artifact's version number.' The defect is confined to the one path-occupancy sentence and the thinness of predecessorV1.role.

The five retainedEvidence members are the five live-cell members in live order, split correctly; namedExecutesLimbs splits the harness cell's two corpus limbs correctly and namedExecutesLimbNote correctly refuses to treat either limb as a retained-evidence member by itself. decision.rule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
decision.recommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL. Do not record as-is. Every custody, digest, verbatim-quotation, leftover-design, required-now, non-satisfaction and non-authorization check passes, and the harness content must be kept exactly as it is. The two repairs are confined to two role strings: state basedOn.predecessorV3.review.verdict's real standing (Claude REJECT 0 blockers / 1 SHOULD-FIX, CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1; Codex not reviewed), and stop claiming this v4 occupies CGHS v4's promised artifactPathWhenAuthored while disclosing what v1 actually is - the file at that path, carrying the byte-equal harness object, holding Claude ACCEPT 0/0 at c2339ec6. A v5 making only those two changes would on these bytes carry no remaining finding known to this reviewer.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: The occupancy remasurement itself is sound and materially better than frozen v3: it pins live HEAD, carries requiredNowUnchanged 28 in agreement with file 08 and leftover-join.v7, quotes the live G01 harness cell and the whole live row byte-exactly, holds leftoverDesign [OBL-2, OBL-D1, OBL-D2] without flipping it, keeps the D-006 unit UNDECIDED without authorizing 26214400, and takes over no neighbouring gate. Twenty-seven of twenty-nine attacks were refuted against live bytes. What it fails on is provenance honesty about its own predecessors, in the one place a reader is least able to check without opening pinned files: it records the REJECTed v3 review as ACCEPT 0/0, and it never cites the v1 review that actually is ACCEPT 0/0 or discloses that v1 sits at the promised path with the byte-equal harness object. The second defect is the unrepaired carry-forward of CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1, whose every premise was re-measured and still holds. Neither defect touches the harness content.

independence: Reviewed against live bytes only. No other reviewer's verdict for this subject was opened. The reviewer's own prior verdicts that this subject pins were re-read from disk and re-measured rather than recalled.
hashDiscipline: Every digest in this verdict was recomputed with sha256 from live bytes at review time. Row and cell equality was tested with == on extracted strings, and harness-object equality with == on parsed objects, not by reading.
